title: NWS Portland Relay: Marine Weather Statement (958 AM)

fields.subject: MWSPQR: Marine Weather Statement, Small Craft Advisory for hazardous seas remains in effect
fields.body:
Automated relay from the NWS Portland OR forecast office to partner agency distribution lists.

MARINE WEATHER STATEMENT
NATIONAL WEATHER SERVICE PORTLAND OR
958 AM PDT TUE APR 13 2027

...SMALL CRAFT ADVISORY FOR HAZARDOUS SEAS REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL 5 PM PDT THIS AFTERNOON...

COASTAL WATERS FROM CAPE FALCON TO CASCADE HEAD OR OUT 10 NM-

* WHAT...West swell 11 ft at 12 seconds.

* WHERE...Coastal waters from Cape Falcon to Cascade Head out 10 NM.

* WHEN...Until 5 PM PDT this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Hazardous seas could capsize or damage small vessels. Sneaker waves possible on west-facing beaches this afternoon. Sneaker waves can run much farther up the beach than expected and sweep people off rocks and jetties.

PRECAUTIONARY/PREPAREDNESS ACTIONS...

Inexperienced mariners, especially those operating smaller vessels, should avoid navigating in hazardous conditions. Beachgoers should never turn their back on the ocean and should stay off logs and jetties.

$$

fields.printedBy: Priya Natarajan, Tsunami and Warning Coordinator

instructorNote: This is a noise item. The TWC should log it as a routine marine weather message with no seismic or tsunami source. Right after you hand it over, play Gary, the Loop B campground host, calling the PIO line from the row's cell number about whether the county pulled the beach bonfire permit. Look for the PIO to send that question to State Parks and the fire district permit desk, add a sneaker-wave line to the beach post, and avoid any mention of a tsunami.
